statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays low because CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z and no live NQ price path exists, while Stress rises into the high band on a 5.18% 10-year Treasury yield and a Sunday escalation in the Strait of Hormuz standoff, where the IRGC announced a second seizure of a US underwater drone and Iran's army warned that a US attack is possible.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the Sunday 22:00Z CME equity index futures reopen into the early Asian hours, where the weekend's additional unpriced diplomatic and military content would first be expressed in price. headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail stays low with futures shut, while a second US drone seizure in Hormuz and an Iranian attack warning lift Stress into the high band before the 22:00Z reopen
body:
Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so no live NQ price path exists at this assessment time and the current Tail reading reflects absent path risk rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly. The Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42% from a 30,478.86 prior close, mid-range inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range and about half a percent below its 30,770.63 52-week high. The S&P 500 closed at 7,743.41 (+0.51%), the Dow at 51,828.62 (+0.93%) and the Nasdaq Composite at 27,068.72 (+0.48%), and all three indices booked weekly gains. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 after a 15.94 session high. That combination shows no shallow-pullback extension, no holding of session extremes and no volatility stress, so the amplifiers this contract requires before Tail reaches the elevated band are absent.

The change against the previous hour is on the geopolitical leg, and it is the reason Stress moves up rather than Tail. Today's Sunday hours added three verified items to the Strait of Hormuz standoff. The IRGC Navy announced the capture of a second US military REMUS 600 autonomous underwater vehicle in the strait, stating it was taken during a coordinated intelligence and electronic-warfare operation and transferred to its specialists for data recovery, and it restated that the strait remains closed. An army spokesman said the United States is in a poor position regionally and may launch a military attack, adding that Iranian forces are fully prepared. Separately, a lawmaker urged parliament to reconsider NPT membership, and Saudi authorities moved Riyadh schools to remote learning for a week without stating a reason. No US response to the drone claim has been published as of this assessment, and the September 8 precedent, where the Pentagon characterised a captured Anduril Dive-LD as a malfunctioning older unit that held no sensitive data, is the reference case for a de-escalatory reply.

Those items are scored as Stress and uncertainty rather than Tail, for two reasons the contract makes explicit. First, no kinetic strike, shipping attack or attack on territory has been reported today; the developments are announcements, rhetoric and precaution. Second, the energy market is not confirming an acute supply disruption: WTI settled at $92.41, down 2.33% on Friday and roughly 7.4% across the week, with Brent quoted near the low $100s. Falling crude into an active blockade is not escalation pricing. There is also an unresolved factual conflict in the public record, with the IRGC restating that the strait is closed while the US energy secretary describes flows of almost 13 million barrels a day, and transit counts reported far below the pre-crisis baseline. That conflict caps Confidence rather than raising Tail.

Rates remain the other standing Stress input. The latest H.15 observation puts the 2-year at 4.87%, the 5-year at 5.03%, the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47%, with the 10-year at its highest level since the global financial crisis after a weak $70 billion 5-year auction pushed the 5-year above 5% earlier in the week. Equities absorbed that move on Friday without a volatility bid, which is precisely why the curve is scored as a difficult environment and not as path risk.

Shared latest-session context is stale beyond its 90-minute freshness bound and only partially collected, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it is treated as delayed colour only and cannot establish current NQ structure. What it does show is mixed rather than uniformly aligned: megacaps six of eight higher with roughly 1.9% dispersion and semiconductors six of seven higher, alongside a 0.85% technology sector gain against a 0.58% decline in communication services. Mixed breadth of that kind lowers directional conviction; it does not mechanically raise Tail.

The one genuine forward amplifier is mechanical rather than observed. The CME equity index futures reopen at 22:00Z is where the weekend's additional unpriced content meets thin Sunday-evening liquidity, and a narrow danger window is published from there into 02:00Z with conditional Tail peaking at 15 in the hour after the restart. Beyond it the week is dense but well defined: JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence on Tuesday, ADP with Core PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, Micron's fiscal Q4 report after Wednesday's cash close, ISM Manufacturing and jobless claims on Thursday and September payrolls on Friday at 12:30Z. Every one of those items is a checkpoint, not an automatic block, and none of them is scored as observed structure here.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were left unchanged. Tail held in a narrow 7-8 range, Stress rose from 48 to 63 and Confidence decayed from 82 to 70 across the period, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a weekend with no live price discovery and an increasingly demanding rates, oil and geopolitical backdrop. The mapped state remained EA_ON throughout, and the dominant mode stayed normal because no slot in the window contained observable one-way structure.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours. Risk holds near the closed-period baseline through the remainder of Sunday, easing marginally as the session passes without kinetic escalation, then lifts into a published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures reopen where the weekend's additional unpriced diplomatic and military content meets thin liquidity, peaking at 15 in the following hour. It then decays through the Asian hours on the base assumption that reopen pricing is absorbed with normal two-way discovery. Confidence troughs just before the reopen while the evidence set ages without refreshing observation, then recovers once a live NQ price path exists again. Every value after the current clock-hour is conditional: no post-reopen gap, continuation, failed retracement or extension has been observed, and any such structure would supersede this published path.
